tasks.spec:
You are the single implementation worker for this task, already selected and already running. Work autonomously to completion: there is no human in the loop, nothing to confirm, and no further model selection to make. Repository documentation about Ringer, orchestration, or agent workflows (docs/, .claude/, AGENTS files, _pm/) describes OTHER workflows, not yours — your only job is the task below. Your current working directory IS a dedicated git worktree of the Marvel Multiverse RPG workspace (the app is a Next.js + TypeScript character builder under apps/marvel). Edit files here directly. NEVER: git commit, git add, git branch, push, install or add dependencies, reformat files you don't need to change, or touch anything outside your owned paths. In particular never edit apps/marvel/src/app/globals.css (another lane owns it): reuse the CSS classes already used in the file you are editing, and if you truly need a new rule, write it under '## Assumptions' in your summary for the orchestrator to add. apps/marvel/AGENTS.md warns that this Next.js version differs from older ones; you are not touching routing, so follow the patterns already in the files you edit. You own only: apps/marvel/src/domain/play/turn.ts,apps/marvel/src/domain/play/turn.test.ts,apps/marvel/src/domain/play/index.ts,apps/marvel/src/features/sheet/SheetView.tsx,fix-summary.md. TWO PLAY-SHEET GAPS, both straight from the Core Rulebook (the project's summary is context/core-mechanics.md, lines about Karma recovery and the conditions table): 1. Start of turn. Ablaze, Bleeding and Corroding each cost 5 Health at the start of the character's turn. Today the sheet shows those conditions as chips with their rules text and the player does the subtraction by hand. Add, in a new pure module src/domain/play/turn.ts exported from src/domain/play/index.ts: startOfTurn(state, sheet) returning { state, losses: { slug, name, amount }[] }. It applies 5 Health per such active condition through the existing adjustResource (so the track's floor holds), returns the SAME state object and an empty list when no such condition is active, and touches nothing else. Poisoned needs a Resilience check each turn, so leave it out and say so in a comment. 2. Karma recovery. Rule: spend 1 Karma and an action, roll Resilience (for Health) or Vigilance (for Focus) against target number 10; on a success recover (Marvel die x rank) + the ability score used, computed just like a damage roll, doubled on a Fantastic roll; no further Karma may be spent on that roll; Bleeding ends on any Health recovery. In turn.ts add: RECOVERY_TARGET_NUMBER = 10; recoveryRoll(sheet, track: 'health' | 'focus') returning a RollRequest of kind 'check' for the right ability (reuse abilityCheck from roll-request.ts and relabel it); and recover(state, sheet, track, roll: D616Roll) returning { state, outcome: 'no-karma' | 'failed' | 'recovered', amount }. With no Karma it returns the same state and 'no-karma'. Otherwise it always spends 1 Karma; it succeeds when resolveCheck(roll, abilityScore, RECOVERY_TARGET_NUMBER) succeeds; the amount comes from damageFor(roll, rank, abilityScore) using the character's RANK as the multiplier (sheet.identity.rank), not a power-boosted damage multiplier, and the plain ability score (sheet.abilities), and is capped by the track's maximum; a Health recovery removes the 'bleeding' condition. Read d616.ts for resolveCheck, damageFor and how the M face counts as 6. 3. SheetView.tsx, smallest change that works: a 'Start my turn' button (exact accessible name) near the conditions panel, with a

that says what was lost per condition in plain words (for example 'Bleeding: lost 5 Health.') or that nothing happened; and on the Health and Focus tracks a button with the exact accessible name 'Spend 1 Karma to recover Health' / 'Spend 1 Karma to recover Focus', disabled when Karma is 0 or the track is already at its maximum, which rolls with the sheet's injected rollDie (rollD616(rollDie)), applies recover(), and reports in a

(or 'Focus recovery') either 'Recovered N Health.' with the dice, or that the check failed and the Karma is spent. Route every state change through the component's existing change() helper so saving and concentration rules keep working. Do not restructure the file, and do not touch the save-failure alert or the phone-width work already in it. HOW TO RUN: from the worktree root run exactly: python3 /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-joe-Agentic-Mini-RPG-Marvel/4ecb59dc-1562-45bb-a475-e78c6af427d7/scratchpad/marvel-tickets/verify.py turn-and-recovery.acceptance.test.ts turn-and-recovery-sheet.acceptance.test.tsx It links node_modules, copies the orchestrator's acceptance tests (turn-and-recovery.acceptance.test.ts, turn-and-recovery-sheet.acceptance.test.tsx) into apps/marvel/src/__accept/, runs the whole vitest suite, tsc, and eslint, prints the tail of any failure, and cleans up after itself. The acceptance tests are the contract; you cannot change them. Read them first: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-joe-Agentic-Mini-RPG-Marvel/4ecb59dc-1562-45bb-a475-e78c6af427d7/scratchpad/marvel-tickets/accept/. The machine is heavily loaded, so a UI test elsewhere in the suite may time out once; if a failure is in a test you did not touch and it passes when you rerun verify, that is load, not you. Add your own tests in src/domain/play/turn.test.ts. OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave your changes uncommitted in the worktree. Write ./fix-summary.md at the worktree root with '# Fix Summary', '## Summary', '## Files Changed', '## Verification' (the verify command and its last lines), and '## Assumptions'. Under 500 words. If you cannot finish inside your owned paths, make no speculative edits and explain the blocker there. Match the surrounding code: terse comments that say why, no new abstractions the task doesn't need, plain-words UI copy with no em dashes.
tasks.verified: the orchestrator's acceptance tests (5 Health per Ablaze, Bleeding or Corroding at turn start with the floor held; Karma recovery = Marvel die x rank + ability, doubled on a Fantastic, capped, Karma spent even on a failure, Bleeding cleared; and the sheet's Start my turn and recovery buttons) pass with the whole suite, tsc and eslint, and only owned files changed — not that the controls sit well on the page
